text:
Patrick Kane came home to Chicago this summer on a two-year deal, and turned 38 on Nov. 19. His first two months back have been strange: plenty of setup work, almost no goals. Saturday's power-play goal in Calgary ended an 18-game drought, which The Athletic's Mark Lazerus called by far the longest of his career.

The passing is intact. He has 13 assists in 20 games, a four-game point streak, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 10.3 primary shot assists per 60 last season, 95th percentile among forwards. The goals were always coming eventually: 2 goals on 5.3 expected, shooting 4.7%.

The harder problem is the team around him. Chicago gets only 39.4% of the 5v5 expected goals with him on the ice, and has scored 5.8 fewer goals than its chances with him out there. Now Connor Bedard is out again with another shoulder injury, his third in less than a year, which puts more of the offense on Kane, Frank Nazar and the kids. Our range has him at 49 to 72 points.
